title: a-sieve-carries-its-band
intention: A sieve carries its band specification — the disk change that makes bands-only inspection structural rather than a remembered policy.
why: Akien, 2026-08-11, correcting CC's framing of his own bands-only ruling: 'bands only should make a disk change shouldn't it? it becomes part of the data attached to the seives, yes?' / 'and prolly in the code that consumes that data' / 'yeah, we gotta have both pieces!' THE LIVED SYMPTOM: today nobody can see a sieve's order without running an AST walk. The band is computed fresh on every run, attached to nothing, stored nowhere — so 'order is the band' is prose, and a reader who wants to know why a sieve fires third has to execute a walker to find out.
traces_to: Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy; 'order is the band' cannot be enforced against a band nothing carries. Law 3 — the band is an unmeasured claim recomputed in flight and never recorded. Law 7 — a stored band with no reconciler would be a record that can silently go wrong; the reconciler is what keeps it loud. Law 1 — the same AST walk is re-derived in every consumer, on every run.

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when all FIVE hold, each by its instrument: (1) each sieve's band is READABLE FROM ITS DECLARATION without running an AST walk — instrument: a command printing every sieve's band from declarations only, with the walker not imported; (2) both consumers read the attached data — instrument: inspector.py:1722 and route.py:189 no longer call reach_of on their own source, verified by grep, with their proofs still green; (3) the reconciler catches a REAL drift — instrument: change a sieve's body so its reach genuinely moves a band, run the reconciler, and it names that sieve, its declared band and its derived band; (4) no second ordering mechanism exists — instrument: grep the declarations for any order/priority/sequence field, expecting zero; (5) A SIEVE IS A MODULE-LEVEL FUNCTION and a declaration that is not one is refused LOUDLY — instrument: point one declaration at a class method and one at a name that does not exist, run the reconciler, and it names both by name rather than banding them 0 (Akien's ruling, see a_sieve_is_a_function). HORIZON: (3) must be a drift from a real edit to a real sieve, not a fixture mutating a declaration to make the instrument fire.

children: none, because the three pieces are ONE SEAM and splitting them lands the half-built state the ruling exists to end. The value written (import_sieve/sieve.py), the value read (inspector.py:1722, route.py:189), and the value re-checked are a single write-read-verify loop: a declaration nothing reads is wrong-intent (d), and a reader with no reconciler is the staleness that killed hand-numbering. Akien named the shape himself — 'we gotta have both pieces!' Referent: the three-file what_conforms of decisions/2026-08-11-one-mechanism-per-meaning.json, which cannot go green on a partial landing.
how: The derivation STAYS where ruling 2026-08-07 put it (import_sieve/sieve.py::reach_of — how far an import looks is that component's own domain) and takes two new jobs: STAMPER, writing the band into the sieve's declaration; RECONCILER, re-deriving to check the declaration still matches. Both consumers stop walking their own source and read the attached data. POLARITY, stated: the tester's (validation_store.source_fingerprint + standing) — MATCH means the declaration still holds, MISMATCH means the sieve's reach moved and the declaration needs an update. NOT the ruling store's polarity, where a match is the failure. OUT OF SCOPE, explicitly: any second way to express order, and any auto-restamp on mismatch (which would make the check vacuous).
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [KILLED] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(does-a-stamped-band-ever-drift) -> PROVED   (KILLED 2026-08-11 — see the KILLED field; the cursor above is where the voyage stopped, kept honest)

watchme.trigger: Every reconciliation — a re-derivation checked against a declaration. An event that fires by construction, since the reconciler is what this ticket builds. No clock, no sweep. Each firing reports per sieve: declared band, derived band, match or mismatch.
watchme.enough: When BOTH shapes have been observed across real use: at least one TRUE mismatch caused by a genuine edit to a sieve's body (the check can bite), and a steady state of matches between (it is not noise). One without the other is not enough — never disagreeing is ceremony, always disagreeing is noise; both are wrong-intent (c) and they are distinguishable only by watching over time. ALSO ENOUGH IN THE NEGATIVE: a mismatch observed being auto-restamped rather than surfaced is wrong-intent (b), and the watch has found the defect it was aimed at.
watchme.carrier: A verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: per firing, the sieve name, declared band, derived band, verdict, and — on a mismatch — what changed in the sieve's body to move its reach. That last field is the payload; a count would be the count-instead-of-names failure probescan exists to end.
watchme.nexus: the import_sieve nexus — the derivation's own growth path, where a widening of DEFAULT_LADDER would be installed. The ladder's comment already says it is 'a first cut (2026-08-06), not a settled taxonomy... Widening it is expected', and a drift this probe observes is exactly that evidence.
